messages:
Maria (sre): FYI - seeing a sustained p95/p99 regression on /v1/generate (model=redwood-l7, region=us-west-2). Started ~08:10 PDT. p95 ~180ms -> 420ms, p99 ~380ms -> ~1.2s. Error rate hasn't changed much (<0.1%), QPS steady. Support ticket #5872 incoming. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/dashboard/latency?route=/v1/generate&region=us-west-2

Priya (oncall): Got it, I'm pulling traces and infra metrics now. Alert fired: `Latency SLI breach: p99 > 1s (5m)` from OpsBot. Will post queries.

OpsBot: ALERT: route=/v1/generate region=us-west-2 p99_latency=1.21s (>1.0s) for 6m. IncidentID=INC-2026-0325-01.

Priya (oncall): Quick checks: no recent cluster restarts in us-west-2, scheduler shows normal pod counts. CPU on inference nodes climbing ~15% over baseline. KV cache hit rate slightly lower (down ~3%). Posting prometheus-ish query I ran:```
# p99 over 5m
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",region="us-west-2"}[5m])) by (le))
```
Result shows jump aligning with 08:10.

Alex (runtime): Any deploys to runtime or models last hour?

Jian (platform): There was a config rollout at 07:58 to increase `max_batch_latency_ms` from 15 -> 30 for better throughput on L7 pools (change id cfg-2026-107). It targeted all us-* pools. Rolling back on a canary would be quick.

Priya (oncall): That matches timeline. Increased batch latency window can increase tail for certain request mixes. But p99 > 1s seems high. Could be batching + larger sequences causing KV cache pressure.

Alex (runtime): Agreed. When batch window grows we see fewer but larger batches; tail can spike if a few requests have long decode times. Two immediate mitigations we can try (low-risk):
1) rollback cfg-2026-107 on us-west-2 only (canary rollback)
2) enable circuit breaker on route `/v1/generate` to drop/queue excess concurrency at the gateway (temporary rate cap)

We should also prepare fallback routing to `redwood-l7-small` (quantized/fast variant) for < 10% of traffic if p99 doesn't improve.

Maria (sre): Support wants a short mitigation playbook we can run now. Priya, can you trigger rollback canary and apply circuit breaker 60s?

Priya (oncall): Starting now:
- Rolling back cfg-2026-107 to previous batch window (15ms) on us-west-2 canary (10% hosts) - command:```
# platformctl roll config cfg-2026-107 --rollback --regions us-west-2 --pct 10
```
- Pushing gateway rule: `/v1/generate` rate-limit to 250 rps and add short circuit (fail-fast after queue 50ms)```
# gatewayctl set-route --route /v1/generate --region us-west-2 --rate 250 --circuit-queue-ms 50
```
Posting temporary monitoring checks: p95/p99 chart + trace sampling at 100%.

Sam (support): I informed the customer that we're actively mitigating and gave an ETA of ~15 minutes. They're receptive to a temporary model fallback if you think that's needed.

OpsBot: ACTION: rollback job started (job id rollback-1760501250).

(10m later)

Priya (oncall): Canary rollback applied to 10% hosts at 08:25 PDT. Gateway rule applied at 08:26 PDT. Early signals: p95 trending down from 420ms -> 240ms, p99 now ~560ms. Traces show fewer large batches and reduced queuing time.

Alex (runtime): Good. Next steps: if p99 stays >500ms after 15m, escalate to full region rollback and/or route 5-10% traffic to `redwood-l7-quant` until we pinpoint root cause. Also need to examine sequence length distribution and per-token decode time.

Jian (platform): We're pulling scheduler logs for any noisy tenants; also checking autoscaler behavior. Not seeing node churn. We'll also snapshot current batching metrics and kernel queue lengths.

Claire (product): Heads-up: some customers on PLG plan might be sensitive to even short regressions. Please keep me posted on fallback usage and any billing implications (falling back to quantized variant might change cost).

Maria (sre): Let's capture a reproducible load profile for postmortem. Repro steps (quick):
1) Use the following script to generate concurrent requests simulating typical RLHF-sized prompts (avg tokens ~600):```
# example using hey or curl loop to reproduce tail
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-l7","input":"<600-token payload>","max_tokens":512}' &
done
wait
```
2) Increase concurrency/variation with k6 or vegeta to exercise batching.

Include a query we used to confirm KV cache pressure:```
# cache hit rate over 10m
sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{region="us-west-2"}[10m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{region="us-west-2"}[10m]))
```
Observed hit-rate dip ~3% at start of regression.

Priya (oncall): After 20m window: p95 ~200ms, p99 ~420ms and trending down. We'll hold the canary for 30m and if stable promote rollback to 100% or try progressive rollback to recover tail completely.

Alex (runtime): Follow-ups for root cause and SLO guardrails:
- Revert global `max_batch_latency_ms` change until we have a workload-aware rollout policy.
- Add SLO-linked automatic circuit (auto-reduce batch window or route to fallback) if p99 > 800ms for 5m.
- Add a protected small-batch path for short requests (seq < 128) to avoid being stuck in large batches.
- Improve metrics: expose per-batch-size latency heatmap and kernel queue length.

Jian (platform): I'll open cfg ticket to add region-scoped rollouts and tagging for risky batch/window changes. Also will add a guard in deploy pipeline that blocks changes to batch parameters if canary traffic contains >20% long-sequence requests.

Claire (product): Please include customer-facing postmortem summary and mitigation timeline. I can prepare a short note for affected customers once we have root-cause.

Maria (sre): Action items and owners:
- Priya: hold canary and either promote or rollback fully in 30m (ONCALL)
- Alex: prepare fallback routing and small-batch path plan (RUNTIME)
- Jian: create cfg/deploy guard tickets and root-cause collection (PLATFORM)
- Sam: keep customers updated (SUPPORT)
- Maria: write initial incident notes + add to postmortem if this becomes an incident (SRE)

OpsBot: Incident INC-2026-0325-01 status=mitigating.

(30m later)

Priya (oncall): Canary promoted to 100% rollback at 08:58 PDT. p95 settled ~190ms, p99 ~320ms. No customer escalations post-mitigation. Closing mitigation window.

Maria (sre): Marking this as mitigated. We'll run a short postmortem with the following sections: timeline, root cause (cfg-2026-107 + workload mix + KV cache dip), mitigation steps, recommended guardrails (deploy-time canary with workload sampling, auto-circuit at p99>800ms, fallback model routing policy), and action owners.

Claire (product): I'll draft customer comms and sync with legal if needed.

Alex (runtime): Follow-up items in Tracker: RD-3421 (small-batch path), RD-3422 (auto-circuit SLO), RD-3423 (batching telemetry heatmap).

Jian (platform): I'll add a pre-deploy check to warn about batch-latency changes and require explicit risk ack.

Sam (support): Noted. I'll update ticket #5872 with mitigation timeline and link to postmortem once ready.

Maria (sre): Thanks all. Closing thread but keeping notes in incident board. If anything regresses, reopen and ping @oncall. :thumbsup:
